Well, it gave me a bit of a fit yesterday on two counts. We bought my daughter a new Dell 2-1 laptop for the remainder of high school and hopefully, college (yeah, I'm giggling a bit at that part as well, but my wife can dream). Came with 10 preloaded. Unpacked it, started the setup, and went through quite a bit of turning things off that I figured she didn't need during the initial account creation. All seemed well. Got her stuff from her old laptop backed up to Google Drive and OneDrive and then started syncing everything to the new laptop. Google Drive worked perfectly, but OneDrive refused to start. I didn't even have an icon in the system tray even though I'd initiated the process. Spent several hours combing the web and cursing louder and louder until I found the answer. I had to unhide hidden and system files and folders and go spelunking into the AppData folder in her home folder and restart the setup for OneDrive. The full path for anyone else who might have this issue is:

C:\Users\username\AppData\Local\Microsoft\OneDrive\OneDrive.exe

Ok. Finally got that part running and her phone pictures and such are now also backing up to the cloud and the computer. Nifty. Then I go to make a USB recovery drive. Fails out. I check the stick for errors. None. I format it. Still fails out. I'll try another stick that I have laying around to see if that's the issue, but if that fails, then I'm going to have to download a plain-Jane .iso and save that to disc or USB. And there's no product key in sight so I'm assuming it's burned into the UEFI or something.

All in all, I'm glad that I had the experience because it's put me off on upgrading my box for the time being. I'm actually finding it to be a little less intuitive than 8.1 in finding what I need to make certain changes, but maybe I'm just not used to it yet.
